title: Operation Mincemeat - most feelgood musical - review
transcript: hello and welcome to theater reviews with Paul Severn I'm here at the fortune theater in a very wet Covent Garden to see operation mince meat this was my first ever visit to the fortune theater because for the last 33 years it's been the home to The Woman in Black now it's hosting operation mincemeat and while that may not match the previous occupants three decade run this polished fast-moving musical comedy certainly deserves a long stay keep watching and I'll tell you why by the way a lot of people have been wondering what this poster design for the show means I mean the whole thing not just the little briefcase handle there um can you see what the designers are trying to put across I'll give you the answer at the end of the review oh and please like comment and subscribe from the moment the yellow curtain goes up on operation Min Suite you know you're in for a treat it begins with a chorus number by the five cast members who start as they mean to go on they fill the stage with their Larger than Life characters exuberant performances and sheer enjoyment of being there over a couple of hours we're told the true albeit embellished story from the second world war of an MI5 plan to use a dead body with fake papers to fool the German Army into thinking the British will invade Sardinia rather than Sicily however this is not really a tribute to MI5 more a satire of male chauvinism in general and the old boy Network in particular operation mincemeat is written and composed by David Felix Hagan Natasha Hodgson and Zoe Roberts developed from an idea to a run at the tiny new diorama theater in London and then polished into a West End show among those on stage right now are all of the creators Les Felix Hagan but plus Claire Marie Hall and Jack Malone who have fantastic seeing voices don't get me wrong the others do sing very well too I'm pretty sure the four understudies were given equal billing in the program are also multi-talented they end up playing many parts of both male and female gender and this adds an additional layer of humor as when Natasha Hodgson playing the group's leader Hugh Montague struts with old Italian entitlement and masculine pomposity um the the his response to the question is it legal is does it matter and tells us for we were made to give the orders while lesser men take heed for some were born to follow but we were born to lead outstanding two is Jack Malone as the secretary Hester who sings the most moving song of the evening dear Bill a letter to a soldier on the front line Zoe Roberts is constantly hilarious as Johnny Bevin the bureaucratic man ultimately in charge and as Ian Fleming the would-be author and our man in Spain the out of his death Hazelden David is a riot as the shy panicking nerdy Charles while Claire Marie Hall excels as the artless young assistant Gene many of the routines seem like classic comedy a musical even for example there's a scene where all five are exchanging and getting tangled in hats phones and a briefcase with Clockwork precision and there are moments of stage magic when they change characters and costumes in the blink of an eye the Caster greatly aided by having director Robert Hasty and choreographer Jenny Arnold on board both a highly experienced and it shows in the slickness of the production and yet operation mincemeat retains the feel and the excitement of a fringe show the theater is one of the smallest in the west end with a stage to match and Ben Stone's set is deliberately sparse with a couple of deaths and chairs a display board and a mobile staircase plus a backdrop that is reminiscent of a map until that is we launch into a very non-fringe-like finale complete with glittering Nazis which really is as glitzy as they announce the songs cross a number of musical genre and the clever witty lyrics are often delivered at the sort of Breakneck speed that may remind you of Gilbert and Sullivan or or Frank Lesser how about this first if we cannot storm the beaches it's sure to spell defeat if the muscle men can't do it call the masters of Deceit in some ways there is a parallel between the small MI5 team that pulled off this unlikely deceit and the small team that created this unexpected West End hit because what we end up with is an incredibly polished laugh out loud Musical and one that deserves to run and run I'm happy to give it five stars oh yes the uh poster artwork well if you haven't worked it out it represents Hitler's hair and mustache clever eh well maybe too clever but I like it and if you worked it out congratulations I hope you found this review interesting and useful if you did please comment like And subscribe to this Channel and you can read my reviews at theater.reviews and if you want to
